item.title: The Wait is Over: Opyn Markets Testnet is LIVE!
item.dc:creator: opyn
item.content:encoded:
After 1.5 years of relentless development and an unwavering vision, we’re thrilled to announce that the Opyn Markets Testnet is officially live on Arbitrum Sepolia!

Perps are one of crypto’s biggest innovations, a unified liquidity layer where capital doesn’t fragment. Yet, today’s perp DEXs aren’t true exchanges. There’s no fungible asset, just synthetic bets built on CEX-like infrastructure. That’s wrong.

Meanwhile, DeFi lending is fragmented for looping and swapping. Uniswap LPs despite deepening liquidity can’t be used as collateral or efficiently hedged. Perps should be composable, not confined.

Everything in DeFi is a perp. Lending/Borrowing, yield bearing stablecoins, Uniswap LPs, Volatility & linear assets.

All should be fungible. All should be composable.

This isn’t just another testnet, it’s the first step in revolutionizing DeFi with a unified trading experience built for composability, efficiency, and power.

Deposit, Borrow, Leverage, Loop, Trade everything in DeFi as perps.

Testnet Phase 0: The Beginning of Something Big

Opyn Markets is designed to eliminate fragmentation in DeFi. To ensure the best experience, we’re rolling out features in phases, starting with:

  • Perpetual Trading — Trade Half-perps, One-perps, and Two-perps with leverage, creating unique, customized trades.
  • Portfolio Margin — Manage exposure across all perp markets using portfolio margin for WETH/USDC pairs.
  • User-Friendly Interface — Easily track funding rates, fees, liquidation health, and more, all within a holistic portfolio management suite.

And this is just the start. In upcoming phases, we’ll be rolling out spot trading, vaults, trade history, and advanced mechanics to create a truly unified trading experience.

Opyn Markets mainnet will be rolled out with a novel system design with lending markets integrated as perps powered by zeroperps. Feel the power of trading linear, squared and half perps and play around with leverage to understand how zero perps unify the lending and borrowing functionalities in Opyn Markets Testnet Phase 0.

Who Can Access the Testnet?

For Phase 0, our most loyal Squeeth users will be the first to access the testnet.

If you’ve been a dedicated Squeeth trader, check your wallets you might already have testnet tokens on Arbitrum Sepolia!

Check eligibility here: https://guild.xyz/opyn-markets.

We will be rolling out access to more users in the coming days. As hinted in previous announcements, OG Squeeth power users will get the first access to the new testnet.

How to Request Access as a New User?

Don’t have testnet access yet? No worries!
➡️ Join our Discord and look out for the “Testnet OG” role to request access to the designated channel and testnet funds.

We’re approving on a rolling basis.

Why Your Feedback Matters

Opyn Markets tackles some of DeFi’s biggest challenges. But to perfect it, we need your insights.

Here’s how you can contribute:
🔹 Dive in: Explore the testnet, try different strategies, and push its limits.
🔹 Share your thoughts: Drop your feedback in discord and let us know how to improve the user experience for mainnet.
🔹 Be part of the journey: Help shape the future of Opyn Markets with us!

Ready to Explore?

The future of DeFi is OPYN-ing up. Join the testnet today and experience a new way to trade, leverage, and innovate.

🚀 Start Testing Now: https://markets.opyn.co/
💬 Join the Conversation: Follow us on X and join our Discord.

Let’s build the next generation of DeFi together. 🚀

item.title: What the F(ungible, **k) are Power perps?
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
In 2024, Opyn claimed that DeFi primitives such as stablecoins, margined futures, and AMMs can be conceptualized as power perpetuals, offering a unified framework for DeFi.

This perspective simplified complex financial instruments into a cohesive design space, enhancing composability and efficiency and led to the impending launch of Opyn Markets.

Let’s break down these concepts to understand how they will operate within Opyn Markets.

If you want to learn the technicalities of power perps and Opyn’s research, you can read more here.

Power perpetuals bring unification to fragmented DeFi markets. By collapsing the barriers between lending protocols, stablecoins, perpetuals, and options, they allow traders to execute sophisticated strategies from a single instrument. Builders can leverage power perpetuals to create novel products, from automated yield vaults to volatility funds, expanding the composability of DeFi systems on Opyn Markets.

What are the different kinds of perps and what do they do?

There’s essentially 4 kinds of perps that act as building blocks of most operations currently done in DeFi.

Zero-Perps (0-Power Perps)

What it does: They aim to track a price of 1 with minimal volatility.

Who should use: Ideal for traders looking to park assets in a stable environment while earning yield-rewards or maintaining exposure to on-chain looping opportunities to maximise returns.

Why do we need it: Zero-perps unify the benefits of stablecoins and perpetual futures, enabling efficient arbitrage and reducing the fragmentation seen between lending and perpetual markets.

Who can build on this: Realistically, if any stablecoin mechanism involves any yield-rewards backed by DeFi operations like lending/borrowing, delta hedging, basis trading, or wrapping, builders can create stablecoins with 0-perps.

1/2 Perps (Square Root Perps)

What it does: Particularly useful for hedging impermanent loss in Uniswap LP positions.

Who should use: These perps allow LPs to hedge risk while maintaining exposure to trading fees in AMMs.

Why we need it: There’s no marketplace to trade Uniswap LP payoffs to hedge for highly volatile trading conditions.

Who can build on this: Protocols looking to make a marketplace for hedging strategies for AMM LP positions or adding wrappers to use LP positions as collateral to make rebalancing more efficient.

1 Perps (Linear Perps)

What it does: Provide linear exposure to an asset’s price, functioning similarly to traditional perpetual futures.

Who should use: Perfect for traders who want direct exposure to price movements with perpetual funding mechanics.

Why do we need it: Linear perps on Opyn Markets are fungible. This means that linear perp positions can now be used as collateral and be mixed with portfolio margined capabilities to hedge risk cheaply or grow exposure exponentially.

Who can build on this: Builders working on leveraged prediction markets can bootstrap liquidity without the need for market makers, long tailed assets facing challenges with market makers and exchange listings.

4. 2-Perps (Squared Perps)

  • What it does: create an options-like convex payoff for any asset without the need for fragmentation of liquidity across strikes and expiries.
  • Who should use: Ideal for trading volatility and capturing trends in trending markets or hedging exposure cheaply across large positions.
  • Why we need it: Long-tailed assets do not have any options markets let alone liquid ones, especially in DeFi. This removes the need to manage a lot of fragmented liquidity across various orderbooks with a unified market.
  • Who can build on this: Builders looking to create strategies with perpetual options, convex trading, volatility or creating exotic payoff markets on digital assets.

Breaking the Fragmentation Barrier

Power perpetuals tackle one of DeFi’s most persistent challenges: fragmentation. Today’s markets divide liquidity across lending, perpetuals, volatility instruments, and LP markets, creating inefficiencies and reducing capital efficiency.

Zero-perps bridge lending and perp markets, offering a stable, predictable environment. 1/2 perps address the gap between LPs and volatility markets, solving impermanent loss risk. 1 perps and 2 perps unify the volatility and directional trading spaces, enabling traders to mix and match exposure seamlessly.

The result? A more efficient, connected market ecosystem where traders and liquidity providers can operate with reduced overhead and increased profitability.

The future of DeFi is perpetual and unified. And it’s just getting started.

item.title: Opyn roads to DeFi.
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
Truly Permissionless. Truly DeFi

The Problem: CEXs and even many DEXs are weighed down by outdated centralized structures , listing teams, market makers, isolated markets, and non-composable positions. These bottlenecks stifle innovation and access.

Opyn Markets breaks free with a permissionless system, enabling anyone to list ERC-20 perpetuals, unlocking true decentralization and composability.

Opyn Markets is rewriting the rules of trading in DeFi with an OPYN permissionless design.

Everything is permissionless. Everything is composable. Everything is possible.

Permissionless Listings: Markets Without Gatekeepers

Select assets. Set parameters. Deploy a Perp Market. It’s that easy.

Opyn Markets eliminates the need for centralized approvals. Anyone can create a market for ANY ERC-20 token, unlocking access to long-tail assets and niche markets often ignored by centralized exchanges. Think Uniswap for Perpetuals: no gatekeepers, just limitless possibilities.

Beyond Market Makers: True Decentralization

Uniswap revolutionized trading in DeFi with AMMs. No listings. No market makers. No trade books. Fungible composable asset positions can be held and interact with directly on a wallet. Opyn is doing it for perps. All kinds of perps.

Think Uniswap but for:

  • Lending Borrowing
  • Perp (swaps) or linear perps
  • Uniswap liquidity provider ERC 721s
  • Perpetual options like exposure via squared perps

ALL IN ONE PROTOCOL.

How does it work?
Deposit assets to Opyn LP market making vaults with stables or other assets. Done.

We’ve packed a lot of tech for adaptive rebalancing of pools to stay efficient with Gradual Dutch Auctions for users to earn APR rewards when the vault makes profits. Users just need to deposit collateral. And it’s done.

Capital efficiency but better.

Deposit. Stake. Loop. Leverage.

Every position on Opyn Markets is fungible. This means it sits like a contract in wallets that interact with these positions on the protocol. Users can use these positions to post more collateral for open positions, use it to loop or leverage APR rewards on vaults or yield-reward bearing zero-perps, and trade these through uniswap pools.

One platform.

Similar credit or collateral rails were only available to institutions in CeFi based on relationships with brokers. In DeFi, users still need to use multiple platforms to loop positions or strategies etc. This allows traders to create custom strategies no matter how complex in a single platform.

Times have changed. Markets are OPYN-ing.

These are the building blocks of an open DeFi ecosystem. This is the next-gen infra to get DEXs to surpass the advantages that CEXs offer today.

  • Developers can launch innovative strategies.
  • Traders access previously unattainable long-tail markets.
  • Liquidity providers achieve higher efficiency and returns.

With no barriers and unparalleled flexibility, Opyn is the DeFi infrastructure of tomorrow.

The Future is Permissionless

Opyn Markets doesn’t just level the playing field, it reinvents it. Whether you’re a trader, developer, or liquidity provider, Opyn’s permissionless, efficient design unlocks new opportunities and redefines what’s possible in decentralized finance.

Ready to explore the next frontier of trading? Try out the Opyn Markets testnet [HERE] and trade on your terms.

item.title: DeFragmenting DeFi: Lending and Borrowing Markets X Yield Generating Protocols.
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
The European Renaissance sparked a revival in art, culture, and intellectual thought, transforming modern civilization. Today, the financial world is undergoing a similar revolution — the DeFi Renaissance. Decentralized Finance (DeFi) uses blockchain and smart contracts to democratize financial services, offering a global, trustless economy without traditional intermediaries. This shift promises to redefine the financial system entirely.

As the industry matures, the DeFi ecosystem faces a mix of challenges and innovations, pointing to a future of increased accessibility to novel financial markets, efficiency, and adoption.

DeFi’s Journey to Maturity

DeFi’s meteoric rise in 2020–21 faced a cooling-off period in 2022 since FTX blew up, drawing liquidity away from the market. This has led to the emergence of industry leaders who found product market fit and have since scaled back DeFi to 2021 levels.

After numerous challenges in 2022, Luna, FTX, multiple hacks, etc, DeFi is holding its ground sternly with TVL levels almost back to 2021–2022 highs.

Despite market challenges innovation did not stop. Projects have found product market fit by developing incentive mechanisms that secure the blockchain and markets that make up DeFi. The yield, this time, is not subsidized by token emissions but is based on interest rates, validator rewards, or basis trades (USDe) & composability within lending and borrowing like loops for borrowing stables for better yielding stables like a current example can be borrow USDC at 12% APY to buy sUSDe to yield 22% APY.

In 2024, a key change has been merging the interest linked markets with lending and trading. Offering flexibility to isolated lending-borrowing platforms to perform more actions with higher functionality.
[Ref ENA and Pendle flywheel → AAVE]

How is the yield source different?

Let’s compare a couple of protocols providing yields in 2022 vs. 2024.

Case Study — Anchor Protocol — Luna ecosystem

Anchor Protocol, which offered almost “risk free” 20% APR, had few standard yield sources. What helped grow the ecosystem to the size it went to was the fixed APR component. Schematically, Luna claimed the yield had 3 sources — interest charged to borrowers with bLUNA borrows for staked LUNA, staking rewards from bLUNA and bETH & liquidation fees.

However, the sustainability of this high yield, particularly the advertised 20% APY, became a critical issue because of the sources being less exclusive. The high yield was largely subsidized by the Anchor Yield Reserve, which was funded by Terraform Labs (TFL) and the Luna Foundation Guard (LFG). When market conditions worsened, the reserve couldn’t keep up with the demand for yield without constant infusions of capital or drastic adjustments to the APY. The Luna — Terraform Labs — Anchor silo was eventually exposed as a ponzi scheme.

What happened?
When market conditions worsened, investors were less inclined to borrow against volatile assets like LUNA because of liquidation risk. This reduced the inflow of new funds from loan interest, thus shrinking one of the yield sources. Conversely, with bear market conditions, many investors sought the safety of high-yield, stablecoin-like assets (UST in Anchor), leading to an explosion in deposits without a proportional increase in borrowing, further straining the yield reserve.

As deposits grew without corresponding borrowing the Anchor Yield Reserve meant to buffer the yield was rapidly depleted. This imbalance was unsustainable, leading to fears of yield reduction or collapse, which in turn contributed to the de-pegging of UST and the subsequent crash of LUNA, collapsing the fake unsustainable yield model that was fueled the ponzi ecosystem for LUNA.

Case Study — sUSDe — Ethena Protocol

When users stake USDe to receive sUSDe part of the backing collateral includes liquid-staked Ethereum (like stETH). The staking rewards generated from staked ETH contribute to the yield. Ethereum’s staking rewards are distributed to those who stake ETH on the Ethereum network. Lido’s stETH yield derives from its launch before validators needed to stake 32 ETH before the merge and were unable to use these funds, Lido helped crowdsource validator setuops for users who wanted to stake smaller amounts and yet receive the staking rewards. Lido wrapped a liquid token stETH that can be unwrapped when Lido unstakes ETH from the set of validators it operates, stETH yield is relatively stable but can fluctuate based on Ethereum’s staking dynamics.

But the majority of Ethena’s yield is backed by perpetual futures funding rates. Ethena uses a delta-neutral strategy where it hedges the staked collateral with perpetual futures. The funding rates from these futures positions, especially when there’s a demand for long positions over short ones, generate additional yield. Historically just the basis trades from holding spot and holding short contracts have generated 10–15% yield for ETH and BTC across major exchanges.

The yield from funding rates can be highly volatile, depending on market conditions. During times of high leverage demand for long crypto positions funding rates can be very high boosting yield. Conversely, in periods where short positions dominate, funding rates can turn negative, though Ethena’s design aims to mitigate this by ensuring sUSDe holders always receive at least zero yield*.

Yield Sources meet Composibility

Basis Yield X Lending Borrowing

When sUSDe is deposited into Aave, it becomes available for lending. Other users can borrow against this sUSDe for a dynamic interest rate. This interest directly contributes to the yield for sUSDe holders.

sUSDe can be used as collateral for borrowing other assets, further integrating it into Aave’s ecosystem. This increases its utility and potential for generating yield through various lending activities. Users can simply lend assets that they hold on AAVE like BTC or ETH, borrow USDC at or USDT at 5–12% and use these funds to buy sUSDe and then lend it again to AAVE.

This creates a looped trade to trade lucrative yields vs lesser ones backed via a delta neutral stablecoin that’s decentralized.

Pendle X AAVE X Ethena

Pendle allows the tokenization of sUSDe’s yield into Principal Tokens (PT) and Yield Tokens (YT).

For context:
PT-sUSDe: Represents the principal of sUSDe, providing a fixed yield upon maturity, thus offering depositors a way to lock in current yield rates.

YT-sUSDe: Represents the future yield of sUSDe. YT holders earn all the yield accrued until maturity, which can be traded or held for speculation on future yield increases.

Users can lend BTC/ETH on Aave and borrow USDT at 5–12% interest and buy into PT tokens that offer a higher APY with a fixed maturity date in case a user wishes to speculate on future yields for the borrowed asset. On top of this,users can provide liquidity to Pendle’s pools, including those with sUSDe. Liquidity providers earn from the trading fees generated on the platform plus additional incentives like Pendle tokens or points from protocols like Ethena for providing liquidity to sUSDe pools.

Speculators can simply trade the future yields or hedge future yields on the base asset like sUSDe. If the market believes in a higher future yield, YT prices might rise, providing an additional layer of yield through market dynamics.

This example of composability in DeFi is very efficient to create unique payoffs for users who wish to use multiple routes or wrappers to do so. The ecosystem now supports the inter-weavedness of spot markets, lending & borrowing markets, decentralised & efficient stables, as well as interest rate markets.

Bottom Line

2022 vs 2024.

Composable, tradeable, leveraged yield. Enter Opyn Markets.

All this can be done in 1 platform with Opyn Markets. More on the optional strategies and more in the next edition.

Opyn Markets is rewriting the rules of trading in DeFi with an OPYN permissionless design. Everything is permissionless. Everything is composable. Everything is possible.

We’re taking sUSDe again to highlight how Opyn Markets can reduce steps to lend/borrow without caps and trade yields. We’re assuming an arbitrary funding rate of zero perp at 10% and sUSDe APY at 25%.

  • Start with 1,000 sUSDe as the base asset.
  • Deposit 1,000 sUSDe into the Opyn Vault to use as collateral.
  • The vault allows you to mint 0-perps by locking deposited sUSDe. In this example,50,000 0-perps are minted.
  • The minted 0-perps are sold on a DEX (like Uniswap), netting 50,000 additional sUSDe.
  • Re-deposit these 50,000 sUSDe back into the vault, drastically increasing your collateral.

Final Position:

  • Long 51k sUSDe (1k original + 50k minted from 0-perps)
  • Short 50k 0-perps

Returns:
25%[sUSDe current APY] * 1k + (25% — zeroPerp funding rate (10%))*50k = 7.75k/1k (deposit) = 770% returns.

The net effect is a leveraged position where there is yield on sUSDe minus the funding rate on the 0-perps. The hypothetical APR calculation could yield up to 770% annualized returns if sUSDe’s APR remains significantly higher than the 0-perp funding rate.

What’s next with Opyn Markets?

Soon DeFi enthusiasts can leverage unified markets like lending/borrowing, perps, convex exposures and AMM LPs. DeFi has already leapfrogged innovation for composability, why not add capital efficiency on top of it to deliver real use cases?

Opyn’s core thesis is that most of the things in DeFi are perps. Lending/Borrowing markets, funding rate or yield reward products, restaked assets and perps have been the core traded products in this space.

In our next edition of Opynomics, we will hint on how liquid perp markets can be beneficial to the overall lending/borrowing space.

item.title: Opynomics: Edition 3
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
DeFi Renaissance with Liquid Staked Rewards?

If you’re reading this, there’s a good chance you trade crypto. Have you ever wondered why in DeFi, with innovations in Liquid Restaking Tokens and reward-bearing stables do we still trade the same ETH/USDT markets vs. stETH/sUSDe?

Binance recently launched BFUSD which provides an APY of approximately 19.55%, allowing users to earn daily rewards by holding BFUSD in their margin accounts without the need to stake or lock funds.

Why is the most commonly traded ETH market on-chain still ETH/USDT instead of stETH/sUSDe?

DeFi leapfrogged the financial markets playbook when Uniswap created AMMs to bootstrap liquidity, removing the need to manage market making via centralized entities. Yet, many perp DEXs reverted to CLOBs (Central Limit Order Books) where the liquidity is still matched with external actors for solving liquidity issues.

DeFi leapfrogged CLOBs to bring AMM design but went back to CLOBs to compete with CEXs?

During this time there have been a lot of successful experiments in reward-bearing stablecoins and Liquid Staking Derivatives (LSDs), which provide instant liquidity via wrappers and pass on the rewards from the base source. LSDs appear to be an efficient form of “money” to get rewards on top of spot holdings that may be inflationary in nature.

DeFi has AMMs. DeFi has LSDs. DeFi has fungibility of contracts. But even with all this infrastructure DeFi’s biggest consumer protocols are competing with CEXs.

Check our previous blog for more on money being debt.

Why LSD Collateral Changes the Game for Day-to-Day Traded Markets

In TradFi, collateral is a static safety net. Assets like bonds or cash equivalents sit idle securing loans or trades but doing nothing else. DeFi has the tools to flip this script by turning collateral into an active participant in day-to-day trading.

Example: stETH (Staked ETH on Lido)
When someone provides stETH as collateral, it doesn’t just secure a trade, it earns staking rewards at the same time.

Pair this with Opyn Markets, and holding assets now becomes extremely efficient.

  1. Efficient Collateral: Backing collateral for margin requirements to an ETH denominated market.
  2. A reward aggregator: Earning staking or lending rewards from activity from minting and selling or buying perps on Opyn Market.
  3. A one-shop hedged position: ETH can be hedged by itself via the linear or squared perp providing efficient hedges without posting overcollateralization in many cases.
  4. Leverage With Efficiency: Use fractional collateral requirements to access greater trading power.

This creates the best of all worlds; a scenario that TradFi struggles to replicate without layers of intermediaries. With tools like permissionless perpetuals, span margin, and flexibility to use reward-bearing collateral, Opyn Markets offers capabilities that even the most advanced TradFi systems can’t replicate.

Beyond TradFi: What’s Possible Only in DeFi?

The flexibility of DeFi platforms like Opyn Markets enables scenarios that would be impossible and mind blowing in TradFi.

Consider this, purely hypothetically, one of the strategy loops possible on Opyn Markets in the following scenario.

We’re taking Ethena’s sUSDe as the base asset. Using it to interact with the 0-perps on Opyn Markets with leverage since the price theoretically should be less volatile. We’re assuming an arbitrary funding rate of zero perp at 10%.

  • Deposit 1k sUSDe
  • Mint 50k 0 perps, sell for 50k sUSDe, deposit into vault
  • User is long 51k sUSDe, short 50k zero perp
  • Returns = 25%[sUSDe current APY] * 1k + (25% — zeroPerp funding rate (10%))*50k = 7.75k/1k (deposit) = 770% returns.

Realistically: This will increase the funding backed rewards on zeroperp, because people will try to arbitrage this irregularity between the base reward-bearing asset as long as the 0-perp funding rate is < sUSDe APY, and theoretically, the minted 0-perps’ rewards should tend to underlying rewards of the leading reward bearing asset in the space.

It’s another synthetic wrapper proving rewards via open-source DeFi code allowing you to access things that have never been possible before.

Use this to create a new market for this wrapped insane LSD stable with a counterpart ETH market for linear perps and maybe your base assets make more rewards passively than your trading strategies.

And there’s more scope to farm yield on top of this. Trade these directly through highly concentrated liquidity pools via FLO while wrapping your assets via AAVE. This means even your leveraged trades can earn yield while being instantly executed.

Moreover, users would be able to run strategies, like basis trading, directly on Opyn Markets.
Let’s compare the same strategy on a CEX or a DEX like Binance or dYdX. Assuming the same arbitrary funding rate of 11% on all platforms.
Binance/dYdX: Deposit 10 ETH, short 10 perps, receive perp funding rate on my ETH (11%) = 1.1 ETH. But users can’t borrow against this position on these platforms.
Opyn Markets: Deposit 10 ETH, short 100 perps, buy 100 ETH. 110 ETH collateral short 100 zero perp collateral. Receive 110*11% =12.1 ETH

More on this in the next edition of Opynomics. Stay tuned!

Such efficiency goes far beyond what traditional financial systems can offer. Instead of copying TradFi’s static models, DeFi embraces the liquidity, composability, and transparency of blockchain to create something better. Reward-bearing collateral doesn’t just improve efficiency; it redefines what collateral can be. All without BANKS.

A Blueprint for the Future

As DeFi evolves, Opyn Markets will show us what’s possible when financial primitives are rebuilt for the digital age. Just as Uniswap revolutionized trading, reward-bearing collateral and tools like 0-perps redefine leverage, risk management, and efficiency.

This isn’t just finance on-chain. This is a blueprint for what’s truly possible in DeFi.

Are you ready to trade on it?

item.title: Opynomics: Edition 2
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
Governments issuing local currency backed stables. Where’s the yield?

Stablecoins like USDT and USDC now command a sizable value of wealth across the crypto market. Tether runs an operation of managing the creation of fiat backed stablecoins, most popularly USDT. It’s very nice to see the wider adoption of stablecoins as a better form of cross-border payments and remittances without the fees. But can stables replace fiat? How is it even possible to buy 1 USDT for 1 USD?

You might have also heard that the UAE recently announced the issuance of a stablecoin backed by the AED. For some background reference, AED is pegged to the USD & currencies like USD have a whole complex mechanism on how that money comes to exist.

Now, this news had a great positive response and people who are users and believers of this tech were supporting this decision. Is it even valuable to hold AED or USD pegged stablecoins? Or is it better to hold money?

Let’s dive into the differences.

Our head of research argues that the fundamental nature of money and why it exists boils down to DEBT.

Money Is Debt?

All money is debt. Money represents a promise from the government to accept it in payments of taxes. A $20 bill is just a piece of paper that the government promises to honor.

In modern economies, money functions as a form of debt, with cash representing a zero-interest loan to the issuing government. When you hold cash, you’re essentially lending funds to the government without earning interest. This loan has no maturity date, and repayment is made in the same currency, meaning the value of your loan remains unchanged over time. Consequently, by holding cash, you forgo potential returns that could be earned through interest-bearing investments.

Under the gold standard, holding currency was like giving the government an interest-free loan of your gold, as you could exchange paper money for gold at any time. To earn interest, you might buy bonds, which could be used directly for transactions or sold for cash when needed. When the gold standard ended, the government stopped exchanging currency for gold, effectively repaying cash with more cash.

The real value lies not in the paper itself but in the trust that people have that the issuing government will back the value of that currency with this interest.

Why Hold Debt Instead of Cash?

Now, if all money is debt, you might wonder why anyone would want to hold cash. The truth is, holding cash has its downsides. For instance, cash is non-yielding. In a world where you can earn interest or yield on your assets, why would you want to hold something that doesn’t grow?

It’s like keeping a pet rock instead of a pet that fetches or maybe holding a Penguin NFT instead of a rat NFT because it gets you more airdrops?

When you consider investments, yield is actually tied to risk. The higher the potential return, the more risk you might be taking on.

Fun fact: One of the lowest, most risk-averse (unless you’re buying contracts issued by SVB1) yields come from overcollateralized interbank lending markets2.

Keeping non-yielding cash might feel safer, but it’s riskier in the long run, especially with inflation eating away at its value. Instead, if you hold debt — like a government bond — you’re effectively holding an asset that has the potential to earn you interest to hedge for the emissions i.e. more supply.

1There are regulations set by central banks mandating that financial institutions are required to hold reserves of an adequate amount of liquid assets, such as cash, to manage any potential bank runs by customers. To remain compliant, those banks with less than the required liquidity will borrow money and pay interest in the interbank market, while those with excess liquid assets will lend money and receive interest. These are usually over-collateralized.

2In March 2023, Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) collapsed due to a bank run triggered by significant losses from the sale of securities, including Treasury and mortgage bonds, which had lost value amid rising interest rates. This led to the bank’s insolvency and subsequent takeover by regulators.

The Role of Stablecoins and Yield

Now, back to stablecoins. If a stablecoin is pegged to something like the AED, it should be yield-bearing.

Why? Because if someone is holding that stablecoin, The AED issues stablecoins for USD, allows some convertibility into USD, and then enjoys the interest rates it receives from the US treasury. The same thing applies to USDC and USDT, of course. SDAI is the arbitrage trade where they take USDC, get cash back from Circle, buy some bonds to generate yield. Someone else is benefiting from the yield generated and users are left holding a non-yielding asset that devalues over time due to inflation.

The market should be structured so that if there’s no yield, arbitrage opportunities would exist to equalize that. For example, if you could earn a better yield elsewhere, people would sell off that stablecoin, pushing its value down until all things which can be converted into each other easily have the same yield.

This is where the connection between yield and price arbitrage comes into play. If there’s a significant difference in yields across similar assets, traders will rush to exploit those differences until prices align. It’s just market mechanics doing its thing!

Remember UST? All Arb Opportunities can and will reflect in a truly fair market. Even if “the peg” stops making sense.

The Illusion of Cash

Let’s dive a bit deeper into why there’s no actual “cash” in a sense. Think about it: paper money is just a representation of value, a promise that can’t really fulfill its purpose if the underlying economy isn’t robust. In fact, with zero-yield bonds (like those the UAE is planning), you’re essentially looking at instruments with no interest payments attached — meaning there’s no borrowing involved, making it inefficient to hold vs money.

Stablecoin issuers usually generate revenue from interest on their reserves, further lending it to institutions and service fees from transactions. This yield is not passed onto holders directly.

If a stablecoin is truly backed 100% by collateral, it should be yielding something. If it’s not, people should look for more yielding sources of money.

The core principles in DeFi, for token emissions resemble what interest rates look like for federal reserve backed currencies a.k.a fiat or money. This ideally should also pass on to stablecoins. Centrally backed stablecoins.

Conclusion: The Future of Money

So, what does this all mean for us? As the financial landscape evolves, understanding these principles — like why non-yielding money doesn’t last and why stablecoins should yield — is crucial. Whether we’re talking about a shiny new stablecoin from the UAE or any other financial instrument, the underlying principles of money as debt and the importance of yield will continue to shape how we think about value.

The next time you pull out cash or consider investing in a stablecoin, remember: it’s all just a big game of debt and trust. And who knows? Maybe one day, we’ll look back and laugh at how we once believed paper money had any real value!

Here’s a recap of Squeeth and why Opyn is transitioning to Opyn Markets

What was Squeeth?

An experiment to create a non-expiring perpetual that tracks ETH as an underlying asset, providing convex exposure without liquidity fragmentation completely on-chain. It was the first ever successful experiment with Power Perpetuals in DeFi.

Since Squeeth’s launch in Jan 2022, the DeFi options market has catapulted from $2-$3 million in combined average monthly premium volume and $20-$30 million monthly notional volume to $10-$15 million monthly premium volume and $700-$800 notional volume in 2024.

In that time, Squeeth attracted over 18,000 unique users that traded more than $1.8 billion in ETH exposure. A single product tracking a single index asset for convex, options-like exposure completely on-chain, achieved this remarkable growth while pioneering non-fragmented liquidity in DeFi.

Since inception, our short-volatility Crab Strategy built on Squeeth has delivered over 50% returns to investors. All of this was achieved organically, with no token incentives to accelerate results.

Now, Opyn is expanding its product suite to support all perpetual traders, driven by a central belief: everything in DeFi is a perp. From this foundation, Opyn Markets will launch a comprehensive power perp suite with TradFi level capital efficiency for traders from all backgrounds.

What is next for Opyn & Squeeth?

Opyn is now transitioning to new product offerings, building to bring users a more comprehensive and agile power perp product suite with Opyn Markets. We’re very delighted to announce that Opyn Markets is targeting to launch in testnet in Q4 2024. The teams at Opyn have been working very hard to research and build something truly extraordinary that will solve multiple current gaps in DeFi.

Opyn Markets is not trying to be the next Binance or compete with CEXs or copy other perp platforms, it’s leveling up to TradFi level capital efficiency and flexibility to allow traders from all backgrounds to coexist in 1 protocol. You can check out what’s truly possible with Opyn markets here.

This shutdown is not a full stop for Squeeth. Squeeth and various versions of Squeeth are possible to co-exist on Opyn Markets. Anyone can deploy new markets for all ERC-20 token pairs across Squared (2-perp), Uniswap LP perps (0.5-perps), stablecoin perps (0-perps), and linear perps in a permissionless manner. Squeeth can coexist with Squ(st)eth (for stETH), Squitcoin (for Bitcoin), Squiniswap (for Uniswap), etc., in this new product suite.

Opyn has also prepared something special for loyal users. Users can expect announcements on future access and rebate incentives along with some surprises. Opyn will share more information about this soon. Keep notification on to stay updated with the latest developments on 𝕏!

How are Squeeth (oSQTH) and Crab users affected?

At shutdown on Nov 4, 2024, 16:00 UTC, all open positions across Squeeth and Crab were closed with no price impact.

The conversion of 1 oSQTH was taken as ~0.032719 ETH per 1 oSQTH at shutdown as per the final settlement rate at 16:00 UTC, November 4th 2024.

Users can now redeem ETH that corresponds to the value in ETH of their position at the shutdown time from oSQTH, Crab, etc anytime from opyn.co.

Detailed Instructions to claim ETH after shutdown are also updated on the frontend of opyn.co.

How did the shutdown affect Squeeth positions?

Users can redeem the converted ETH from opyn.co/Squeeth from all products built on top of Squeeth.

For Zenbull users: Because of the March 2023 Euler hack, which impacted the ZenBull contracts, specific actions were taken to ensure that any remaining assets in the Zen Bull contract are still available to withdraw post Squeeth shutdown. Users can learn how to claim CRAB from the Zenbull strategy contract here.

For oSQTH LP holders: LP tokens in vault can be claimed from Squeeth LP frontend. Users who have LP positions can withdraw their positions to Uniswap to claim oSQTH and redeem oSQTH for ETH here. All LP positions have been rebalanced and all underlying oSQTH exposure has been converted to ETH at shutdown.

For Long or Short oSQTH positions: Users can now redeem ETH that corresponds to the value in ETH of their position at the shutdown time from oSQTH, Crab, etc anytime from opyn.co. Users can also check this detailed guide on redemptions here.

Have more questions or need assistance?

Visit Opyn’s Discord and ask questions in the “👴 Squeeth-retirement” channel. If you want to know more about the rebalances and calculations, please refer to the FAQs here.

Stay tuned for updates on our next phase, with Opyn Markets.

item.title: Opynomics: Edition 1
item.dc:creator: Shark
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Opynomics: Edition 1 — your weekly glimpse into the unfiltered thoughts and candid conversations of the Opyn team.

The Opyn team discusses the latest happening on Crypto Twitter and the broader Web3 institutional space to discuss everyone’s opinions on certain things. We thought why not share all these hot takes with the wider community to get your thoughts on these topics as well.

As a result, Opynomics has emerged as a weekly roundup of the latest most-talked topics with our unfiltered thoughts.

Please note: This roundup is a collection of our personal reflections and discussions and should not be taken as investment advice. So, join us as we navigate the complexities of decentralized finance, share our insights, and perhaps even stir up some intriguing questions along the way. Let’s dive in!

Navigating Tech, Regulation, and the Inevitable March Forward

You know, I was just reading about that Tornado Cash situation. So, a court decides that their free speech defense doesn’t hold up because software code isn’t covered by the First Amendment. Makes you think, doesn’t it? If a U.S. court were to tackle the same issue, would they rule differently? Maybe the U.S. will decide to take direct action instead of letting European jurisdictions handle it.

It’s like that Telegram guy who got into hot water over his crypto project. Perhaps if there’s a similar case in the U.S., we might see a different outcome. At the heart of it all is this fundamental argument about privacy in financial transactions. I mean, making a transaction is a form of communication, right? Placing an order expresses intent — it’s conveying information between parties.

When DeFi — decentralized finance — really gets up to speed, being fast, competitive, secure, and efficient, all these debates might become moot. You can’t stop people from communicating more efficiently. It’s like trying to ban torrents back in the day. Remember how hard they tried to shut down file-sharing? Didn’t quite pan out. DeFi is aiming for that same resilience — a system that’s tough to suppress because it’s just plain better.

There’s always this anti-tech sentiment whenever something disruptive comes along. People worry about losing jobs or the tech being used maliciously. Sure, there are risks, but stifling innovation over fear seems shortsighted. Trying to regulate algorithms? That’s a slippery slope. Everyone wants to have their say, to stake their claim in these new spaces, but you can’t stop progress by throwing up roadblocks.

Think about past tech revolutions. The textile industry, for instance. When machines started doing the work of manual laborers, there was serious pushback. The Luddites even destroyed machinery to protest. But could they stop the industrial revolution? Not a chance. Innovators often faced trouble — sometimes legal, sometimes worse — but technology kept advancing.

Or take the advent of automobiles. Early car makers faced all sorts of regulations, like speed limits barely faster than walking pace and requirements to have someone walking ahead of the vehicle waving a red flag. It sounds ridiculous now, but back then, it was serious business. Innovators pushed through, though some paid hefty prices for challenging the status quo.

Here’s another one: imagine if we had a box that could transform soybeans into cars. We send soybeans to Japan, and out come cars. Some folks would debate whether we should use such a technology, questioning the impact on jobs, the economy, whatever. But in the grand scheme, most would agree that benefiting from such an innovation beats sticking to old ways.

Even with opposing views, if something offers a net good, it usually prevails. Being anti-trade or anti-tech doesn’t stop the world from turning. Technology keeps marching forward, and while it’s important to address legitimate concerns, halting progress isn’t the answer. Maybe instead of throwing up barriers, we should be figuring out how to adapt and make the most of what’s coming.

In the end, you can’t stop people from building new, disruptive technologies. It’s like trying to hold back a river with your bare hands. Better to grab a paddle and figure out how to navigate the currents. Thoughts?

Crypto as Collateral

So, I was catching up on the news, and guess what? The CFTC — you know, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission — is reportedly considering accepting digital assets like crypto as trading collateral. It’s about time, right? I mean, they already let folks use stocks as collateral, so allowing crypto seems like the next logical step. It just makes basic sense.

But you have to wonder, is there some kind of financial repression going on? Are they hesitant because they want to keep a tight grip on the financial system? If they don’t allow crypto as collateral, it’s kind of a setback for the whole crypto space. But fundamentally, if you can manage the risks and handle liquidations efficiently, it should be all good.

This whole situation reminds me of how new technologies often get the short end of the stick before they’re accepted. Take the early automobile industry. Innovators like Henry Ford faced all sorts of obstacles — regulations, pushback from the horse-and-buggy folks, even legal troubles. People were skeptical, and some cities had laws that made it nearly impossible to drive a car. But look where we are now.

Or think about the dawn of the internet. Early pioneers pushed boundaries, sometimes stepping on legal toes because the laws hadn’t caught up yet. Companies like Napster got into serious legal hot water for disrupting the music industry. They faced lawsuits and regulations, but their innovations paved the way for how we consume media today.

Even the aviation industry had its hurdles. The Wright brothers had to deal with patent wars and government indifference. Innovators often find themselves in sticky situations because they’re charting unknown territory.

So, with the CFTC mulling over crypto as collateral, it’s the same old song and dance. New tech emerges, regulators scramble to make sense of it, and the pioneers sometimes get caught in the crossfire. But if history tells us anything, it’s that progress usually wins out in the end.

If the risks are manageable and the systems are in place, accepting crypto as collateral could be a big win — for both the financial industry and the broader adoption of digital assets. Sure, there might be bumps along the way, but that’s just part of the journey.

In a few years, we might look back and wonder why this was even a debate. Until then, we’ll keep an eye on how things unfold — and maybe grab another drink while we wait for the next big thing to shake things up.

Crypto and Taxes

So, get this — I heard Ohio is thinking about accepting cryptocurrency for tax payments and fees. Yeah, you could actually pay your taxes with Bitcoin or something. It’s kind of wild when you think about it. You know how for a currency to really hold value, people — and especially governments — need to accept it? Taxing in the same currency closes that loop. It could be a big step in defining crypto as a legitimate currency.

But here’s the thing: even if Ohio starts taking crypto for taxes, the base asset everyone’s measuring everything against is still the U.S. dollar. So, is crypto really becoming its own thing, or is it just another way to move dollars around?

This reminds me of the “fiscal theory of the price level.” Basically, it’s this idea in monetary theory that the value of a currency is backed by the government’s fiscal policy — like its spending and taxing decisions. In a way, currency acts like a security against inflation. So if a state starts accepting crypto for taxes, does that make crypto more stable or valuable? Maybe, maybe not.

We’re in this interesting spot where we’re going to get a lot more data in the next few years. It’s like we’re all part of this big experiment, and things are moving faster than ever. We’ll see what works best and what doesn’t when it comes to integrating crypto into everyday life.

New tech emerges, regulators scramble to catch up, and sometimes the innovators get caught in the middle. But if history tells us anything, it’s that progress usually wins out in the end.

We’ll have to wait and see how this plays out. Maybe accepting crypto for taxes will legitimize it further, or maybe it’ll just be a blip on the radar. Either way, we’re about to learn a whole lot about how crypto fits into our financial system. In the meantime, let’s kick back and watch how this grand experiment unfolds. Who knows? In a few years, paying taxes in crypto might be as normal as swiping a card.

WEF’s ‘Sandbox-First’ Approach: Playing Nice in the Crypto Playground

So, get this: the World Economic Forum is all about this ‘sandbox-first’ approach for DeFi adoption. Imagine regulators and innovators playing together in a sandbox, building castles without stepping on each other’s toes. Sounds almost too good to be true, right?

While the EU seems to be tying itself in knots with red tape, places like China & UAE are setting up special zones to experiment with DeFi. It’s like they’re hosting their own exclusive crypto parties! Just this week the UAE government announced that they are launching a AED pegged stablecoin that can act as a regulated anchor for facilitating efficient transactions in a global hub like Dubai but also have compliance checks in place so that the bad actors don’t indulge in funny business.

A lot of nascent regulations across the space are adding VPN checks. Sure, adding VPN checks to DeFi feels a bit like putting a leash on a wild horse. But hey, if it keeps the regulators happy without killing the vibe, maybe it’s worth a shot.

It seems like every leading global economy has a different take on what it means for regulators. Different strokes for different folks — or in this case, different countries trying out their own crypto recipes. Beats having a bland, one-size-fits-all regulation, don’t you think? How it actually shapes up would be worth exploring nonetheless.

As a community with giga-brain financial leaders in a more tech-savvy nascent environment, we should advocate more on what would collectively help bridge the gap between the regulators with the DeFi ecosystem. We should collectively put more thought into keeping the DeFi spirit alive while making sure the party doesn’t get shut down by the fun police? No?

The Supermeme Cycle: Rethinking Value and Liquidity in Modern Finance

I guess everyone is now talking about Murad and memecoins this past week. Is the Supermeme cycle in the room with us?

Every currency functions as a collective agreement among people who believe in its value, making even the most established currencies similar to meme coins in essence. This shared delusion, or mutual trust, is what gives money its purchasing power and facilitates trade.

Extending this perspective beyond currencies, assets like houses, stocks, and gold are also tokenized forms of value. Their worth is not intrinsic but is derived from the collective confidence that they hold value. For instance, while an apple has immediate utility as food, its capacity as a medium of exchange is limited compared to a stock or a currency note.

Interest rates can be likened to token rewards within this framework. They serve as incentives, encouraging participation and investment within financial systems, much like rewards in digital token ecosystems.

In the realm of cryptocurrencies, price volatility often takes a backseat to liquidity. The ability to hedge positions and move freely between assets underscores the importance of liquidity over price. The core thesis suggests that the value of tokens is pegged to the liquidity of their underlying assets; liquidity is what creates and sustains value (or what I’ve been told by anon giga-brains that understand this much better than me).

This perspective reveals that meme coins are simply more exaggerated versions of existing financial instruments.

So let us know? Is everything a memecoin? Am I a memecoin?

Well, folks, that’s a wrap for this week’s Opynomics. It’s been a roller coaster, and I, for one, am excited (and a little nervous) to see where we go from here.

Before you head out, I’d love to hear your thoughts. What’s the most intriguing or puzzling thing you’ve come across in the DeFi space lately?

Remember, in the world of crypto, the only constant is change — and maybe the occasional meme coin.

Cheers, and see you next week!

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed in this weekly roundup are lighthearted and personal reflections of the individuals involved. They are intended for entertainment purposes only and do not represent the official views or positions of Opyn. Please do not consider any of this content as professional or investment advice.

Squeeth. Squeeth. Squeeth. A lot of people are talking about the Squeeths! But what market conditions are the best time to Squeeth? This article explains the ideal market conditions to:

  • Zen Bull
  • Crab Strategy
  • Long Squeeth

To Squeeth 👉 https://go.squeeth.com/BestConditions

Squeeth review

Squeeth is a DeFi-native derivative that gives exposure to the squared price of ETH. Owning oSQTH has a payoff that increases quadratically as the ETH price increases. It’s a way to make a leveraged bet on ETH, where leverage increases as the price increases, WITHOUT liquidations.

oSQTH, the token that represents Squeeth, is a fungible ERC20 token, enabling it to be traded separately (in uniswap pools or as collateral for loans). This composability is a major advantage to Squeeth’s design. It also allows Squeeth to be used as infrastructure for DeFi-native structured products such as Crab and Zen Bull!

For an in-depth explanation of Squeeth, check out the Squeeth Primer.

Zen Bull Strategy (Stack ETH Strategy)

  • Payoff Profile: Smooth curved line with an ETH stacking bubble!
  • Income: ETH returns come from the daily premium paid by Long Squeeth holders
  • Max Gain: Unlimited
  • Max Loss: Limited (amount of ETH deposited)
  • Liquidation: While it’s possible for Zen Bull strategy positions to be liquidated, it’s less likely due to automatic rebalances (MWF) and price-based rebalances for 20% ETH price moves.

Ideal Market Condition to Zen Bull

The Zen Bull strategy is ideal for calmly-rising ETH market conditions during periods of low ETH price volatility (when the price of ETH is calm!).

Specifically, Zen Bull does best when Squeeth realized volatility is less than Squeeth implied volatility (when ETH is calmer than the Squeeth market expects). Zen Bull is a ‘long delta’ ‘short volatility’ position.

The Zen Bull Strategy automatically manages user ETH deposits to create a position with a 1:1 exposure to the price of ETH (approximate delta of 1).

The Zen Bull strategy aims to be profitable in ETH terms (stack that ETH!). The strategy earns returns through sustainable methods (selling oSQTH) vs. DeFi methods such as yield farming where returns dry up quickly. Zen Bull = real yield.

Metrics to Pay attention to:

Current Zen Bull Profit Threshold (Price Bands):

  • The most important consideration before depositing in the Zen Bull Strategy is Zen Bull’s profitability threshold (the price bands). If you deposit into the Zen Bull Strategy when the price bands are tight & subsequently withdraw when the price bands are wide, you are effectively selling Squeeth when it’s inexpensive, and buying it back when it’s expensive. Selling low & buying high is not a good look!
  • The Zen Bull profitability threshold indicates the ETH price range between rebalances that would result in a profitable period.
  • The profit threshold is based on Squeeth’s current Implied Volatility (premiums). The Zen Bull strategy would be unprofitable if ETH moves more than approximately the profit threshold in either direction before the next rebalance (MWF)

Risk:

The two biggest performance risks for Zen Bull Strategy deposits are:

  • If you deposit into the Zen Bull Strategy when the price bands are tight & subsequently withdraw when price bands are wide
  • If ETH moves more than approximately the profit threshold (price bands) in either direction between rebalances.

While Zen Bull Strategy deposits can be liquidated, automatic rebalancing on a time-based or ETH price changes threshold helps prevent a liquidation from occurring.

To deposit in Zen Bull, go to https://go.squeeth.com/BestZB

Crab Strategy (Stack USDC Strategy)

  • Payoff Profile: Upside down smile 🙃 (i.e. a hill, and you stack the most USD when you’re on top of the hill)
  • Income: USD returns come from the daily premium paid by Long Squeeth holders
  • Max Gain: Unlimited
  • Max Loss: Limited (amount deposited)
  • Liquidation: While it’s possible for crab strategy positions to be liquidated, it’s less likely due to automatic rebalances (MWF) and price-based rebalances for 20% ETH price moves.

Ideal Market Condition to Crab

Crab Strategy is ideal for sideways market conditions (crabs move from side to side, get it?!) when the price of ETH fluctuates within a relatively stable range with periods of low volatility. More specifically, the Crab Strategy does best during periods when Squeeth realized volatility is less than Squeeth implied volatility.

The Crab Strategy automatically manages user USDC deposits to create a position with neutral exposure to the price of ETH (approximate delta of 0).

Crab strategy aims to be profitable in USD terms. The strategy earns returns through sustainable methods (selling oSQTH) vs. DeFi methods such as yield farming where returns dry up quickly. Crab = real yield.

Metrics to Pay attention to:

Current Crab Profit Threshold (Price Bands):

  • The most important consideration before depositing in the Crab Strategy is Crab’s profitability threshold (the price bands). If you deposit into the Crab Strategy when the price bands are tight & subsequently withdraw when the price bands are wide, you are effectively selling Squeeth when it’s inexpensive, and buying it back when it’s expensive. Selling low & buying high is not a good look!
  • The Crab Strategy profitability threshold indicates the ETH price range between rebalances that would result in a profitable period.
  • The profit threshold is based on Squeeth’s current Implied Volatility (premiums). The Crab Strategy would be unprofitable if ETH moves more than approximately the profit threshold in either direction before the next rebalance (MWF)

Price Impact + Slippage

Negative price impact and slippage happens when a trader makes a trade, and the price is higher or lower than expected (for both buying and selling). To combat negative price impact and slippage, Opyn launched Jumbo Crab, a mechanism that allows users to make LARGE deposits into crab with better pricing and significantly less slippage!

Risk:

The two biggest performance risks for Crab Strategy deposits are:

  • If you deposit into the Crab Strategy when the price bands are tight & subsequently withdraw when price bands are wide
  • If ETH moves more than approximately the profit threshold (price bands) in either direction between rebalances.

While Crab Strategy deposits can be liquidated, automatic rebalancing on a time-based or ETH price changes threshold helps prevent a liquidation from occurring.

For more details on Opyn’s Crab Strategy, check out this article.

To deposit in Crab, go to https://go.squeeth.com/BestCrab

Long Squeeth

  • Payoff Profile: ETH²
  • Cost: Daily Premium
  • Max Gain: Unlimited
  • Max Loss: Limited (amount deposited to buy oSQTH)
  • Liquidation: Long Squeeth CANNOT be liquidated

Ideal Market Condition to Long Squeeth:

The ideal market condition to buy Squeeth is when a trader has conviction in the upward price movement of ETH in the short to medium-term. Squeeth (short for squared ETH) supercharges ETH, giving the derivative an ETH² payoff.

Metrics to Pay attention to:

Squeeth Implied Volatility (IV):

  • The most important consideration before going long Squeeth is Squeeth’s current implied volatility.
  • Implied Volatility is a forward-looking metric designed to gauge how volatile the market may be in the future (high IV signals large price swing is ahead, low IV signals price will remain stable).
  • Comparing current Squeeth IV to Reference Vol or historical Squeeth vol can help determine if it’s a relatively expensive / inexpensive time to buy.
  • Ideally you would buy Squeeth when IV is low & subsequently sell when IV is high , (i.e. buy Squeeth when it’s inexpensive, and sell it when it’s expensive)
  • If you buy Squeeth when IV is high & subsequently sell when IV is low, you are effectively buying Squeeth when it’s expensive, and selling it when it’s cheap. Buying high & selling low is not a good look!
  • Note: IV indicates the market’s view of volatility, but it is not indicative of future IV levels.

Premium:

  • Squeeth tracks rather than equals ETH² because longs pay a daily premium (in-kind funding) to shorts to maintain the position.
  • The premium of Squeeth is directly related to Squeeth’s Implied Volatility (high Squeeth IV = high daily premium, low squeeth IV = low daily premium)

Risk:

Pay attention to Squeeth premiums throughout the period that you hold Squeeth. Holding a Long Squeeth position for an extended period (> 1 year), during which ETH trades sideways or goes down in value, will cause a loss in ETH² exposure due to the daily premium paid to Squeeth sellers.

Compared to a 2x leveraged position, Squeeth will make more when ETH goes up and lose less when ETH goes down, but premium rates are expected to be higher due to exposure to pure convexity (ETH² payoff).

If you buy Squeeth, what affects oSQTH Performance? Read this thread.

To buy Squeeth, go to https://go.squeeth.com/BestConditions

About Opyn

Opyn is building DeFi-native derivatives and options infrastructure. Opyn’s product Squeeth (squared ETH) is a new financial derivative that gives traders perpetual exposure to ETH².

Summary

Opyn’s Zen Bull allows users to stack ETH returns with one click.

The strategy focuses on ETH accumulation. DeFi’s open ecosystem of programmable “money legos” makes this possible in a crypto-native way.

It combines Crab with a lending protocol to earn additional ETH returns when Squeeth volatility is lower than expected.

Zen Bull stacks ETH when ETH is calmer than the Squeeth market expects.

Ideal Market Condition to Zen Bull

The Zen Bull strategy is ideal for moderately-rising ETH market conditions during periods of low ETH price volatility (when the price of ETH is calm!).

Specifically, Zen Bull does best when Squeeth realized volatility is less than Squeeth implied volatility (when ETH is calmer than the Squeeth market expects). Zen Bull is a ‘long delta’ ‘short volatility’ position.

The Zen Bull strategy does best when Implied Volatility is above Realized Volatility.

Additional Zen Bull Value Propositions:

  • 0 management fees
  • The Zen Bull position is 24/7 liquid and users can deposit or withdraw at any time (deposit and watch or actively trade!)
  • Zen Bull is an ERC20 token, which means it can be traded on Uniswap, used in Uniswap Pools, or used as collateral for loans (like Crab!)

Under The Hood

The goal of the strategy is to earn additional ETH returns, while maintaining a high ETH exposure (or delta) of around 1.

User ETH deposits are split between the Crab Strategy and lent on Euler to achieve:

1. ETH Returns from Crab’s short oSQTH position.

2. Leveraging up by borrowing USD and buying more ETH to increase ETH exposure on Euler.

These two components are combined to create a position that earns additional ETH returns, while also maintaining positive exposure to the price of ETH (a bullish delta of ~1).

Explaining Zen Bull’s Delta of 1:

The objective of the Zen Bull is to maintain an approximate delta of 1.

A delta 1 position’s goal is to have a one-to-one relationship with the underlying asset in terms of price movements. In other words, when there’s a change in the price of ETH, you would expect the Zen Bull price to move in the same direction and with a similar magnitude as ETH.

The goal of the Zen Bull strategy is to earn additional ETH returns from Crab, while maintaining a high ETH exposure (or delta) of around 1.

The Crab strategy’s delta is 0 (on average), so the ETH exposure in Zen Bull comes only from the ETH collateral in the Euler loan.

Equity in the strategy is assets minus liabilities. In Zen Bull’s case, assets include Crab tokens and ETH collateral in the loan, while the liability is the USD loan.

Rebalancing to Maintain an Approximate Delta of 1

There are two factors that mean the Zen Bull Strategy must be rebalanced.

Maintaining Delta 1

  1. If the price of Crab increases, the delta of Zen Bull decreases. The strategy must either (a) buy more ETH (borrow USDC, buy more ETH) or (b) withdraw some ETH from Crab so that the Zen Bull strategy delta returns to 1.
  2. If Crab goes down in dollar value P, the Zen Bull delta increases. The strategy must either © sell some ETH on the loan side and repay USDC or (d) deposit some ETH from the loan component (on Euler) in Crab so that the Zen Bull strategy delta returns to 1.

Maintaining The Collateralization Ratio

To understand levers impacting Zen Bull’s collateralization ratio, here’s a few examples:

  1. If the ETH price decreases (and Crab price stays the same), the Zen Bull strategy could withdraw ETH from Crab, sell to USDC, and repay some of its outstanding loan to return Zen Bull’s collateralization ratio to 200%.
  2. If the ETH price goes up (and Crab price stays the same), the Zen Bull strategy could borrow USDC to buy ETH and subsequently deposit ETH into Crab to bring the collateralization ratio back to 200%.

Explaining the Zen Bull Rebalances:

The strategy rebalances every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday after the Crab Auction. There is also a price-based rebalance in case the Zen Bull must be urgently rebalanced based on extreme changes in the price of ETH.

There are two ways to rebalance:

  1. Leverage Rebalance:
  • The loan component of the Zen Bull consists of ETH collateral and USD debt. If the strategy can achieve an accepted delta by buying or selling more ETH against its current loan while maintaining an acceptable collateralization ratio range of 180% — 220%, this is the preferred method of rebalancing for the strategy since it will avoid a higher rebalance cost). Leverage Rebalance help set delta to 1, but changes the collateralization ratio, which is a healthy level as long as the collateralization ratio is within 180% and 220% immediately before the next rebalance.

2. Full Rebalance:

  • If a leverage rebalance is not possible, the strategy will perform a full rebalance with a separate Crab Auction rebalance and a rebalance of the loan component of the strategy. A full rebalance will only happen if a leverage rebalance cannon happen due to the collateralization ratio being too high or too low (outside of the 180% to 220% range), but does set delta to 1 and cr to 200%.

Zen Bull vs. Crab vs. Long Squeeth vs. Long ETH

Deciding between Zen Bull, Crab, Long Squeeth, and Long ETH? Let’s look at the market considerations for each:

Long Squeeth 🐱

Ideal market condition:

  • When the price of ETH increases a lot in a short amount of time
  • When you want leverage *without* the possibility of being liquidated
  • Long Squeeth (short for squared ETH) supercharges ETH, giving the derivative an ETH² payoff

Long ETH

Ideal market condition:

  • When the price of ETH increases, either rapidly or slowly
  • Hold without having to think about liquidation risk or actively trading

Zen Bull Strategy 🧘‍♀️🐂

Ideal market condition:

  • When you want ETH+ returns
  • When the price of ETH increases calmly within a range (non-volatile, without large spikes up or down)
  • When you want to earn additional ETH returns (yield) with positive exposure to ETH (delta = 1)

Crab Strategy 🦀

Ideal market condition:

  • When you want USD returns
  • During a sideways market (delta = 0), when the price of ETH is calm (non-volatile, without large spikes up or down)
  • When ETH is rangebound

Zen Bull Risks

There are 4 main risks for Zen Bull Strategy depositors:

  1. Depositing into Zen Bull when the current profit threshold is low (~3%) & subsequently withdrawing when the threshold is high (~7%), effectively sells Squeeth when it’s inexpensive, and buys it back when it’s expensive! In other words, if you deposit when the price bands are tight / narrow, and withdraw when they are wide, this will have a negative effect on PnL.

2. If ETH moves more than approximately the profit threshold in either direction between rebalances. i.e. When the price of ETH is CRAZY up OR down (when ETH is volatile). the strategy may be unprofitable.

The Zen Bull Strategy earns ETH if ETH moves LESS than x% up or down between rebalances (the profit threshold). The Zen Bull strategy is ideal for moderately-rising ETH market conditions during periods of low ETH price volatility (when the price of ETH is calm!).

3. If the Zen Bull Strategy falls below the safe collateralization threshold (200%), the strategy is at risk of liquidation.

If the Zen Bull Strategy falls below the safe collateralization threshold of 200%, the strategy is at risk of liquidation. However, automatic rebalances reduce the likelihood of liquidation for depositors.

4. Transaction fees, rebalancing costs, and slippage can cut into profits.

The automatic rebalances that maintain positive exposure to the price of ETH (delta ~1) can reduce Zen Bull strategy returns because of transaction costs to rebalance. Additionally, Price impact due to low liquidity can reduce crab profits when depositing / withdrawing.
